scope: Persistent artifact catalog design; Windows ingestion; publication; bounded reuse; invalidation
implementation_status: Design research. Recommendations are not implementation or performance claims.
method: Read preserved 0.10 handoff/agenda; targeted system2 discovery then system1 primary-source verification; opened selected paper and specification sections. No paywalled sources or secondary summaries used as factual support.

sources.title: C++ working draft: atomic<shared_ptr<T>>
sources.verified_fact: Shared-owner load/store/exchange and comparison are atomic; lock-free availability is implementation-defined; initialization is not an atomic operation.
sources.project_application: Use synchronized immutable-owner publication; prefer a simple mutex initially. Do not claim lock-free reads without checking the implementation.

sources.title: ReadDirectoryChangesW
sources.verified_fact: Overflow can discard notifications and return success with zero transferred bytes; reconstruct changes by enumeration. Asynchronous completion obtains byte count separately.
sources.project_application: Treat event streams as dirty hints with explicit reconciliation on overflow/restart; never equate zero details with no changes.

sources.title: Using the Change Journal Identifier
sources.verified_fact: USN records are scoped to a journal identifier; the identifier can change after unusable history or recreation. The documentation describes administrator privilege requirements.
sources.project_application: Persist journal ID plus cursor, verify continuity, retain explicit capture as an ordinary-user fallback.

sources.title: READ_USN_JOURNAL_DATA_V0
sources.verified_fact: A requested StartUsn older than the first retained USN produces ERROR_JOURNAL_ENTRY_DELETED.
sources.project_application: Recover by reconciliation when history is no longer available; a cursor is not an everlasting complete log.

sources.title: FILE_ID_INFO
sources.verified_fact: The volume serial number and 128-bit file ID identify a file for comparing open handles.
sources.project_application: Use handle identity as supporting metadata; pair with content identity and a generation.

sources.title: CreateFileW
sources.verified_fact: Sharing flags govern conflicting opens; denying write sharing can fail on existing writers. OPEN_REPARSE_POINT changes whether a symbolic link or its target is opened.
sources.project_application: Use one handle per capture and explicit link/sharing policy. Do not claim arbitrary concurrent-tree capture becomes transactional.

sources.title: Case Sensitivity
sources.verified_fact: Windows supports per-directory case sensitivity; unconditional case conversion can misaddress files in such directories.
sources.project_application: Preserve relative path spelling and document case policy; reject ambiguous normalized keys.

sources.title: ReplaceFileW
sources.verified_fact: REPLACEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH is documented as unsupported; replacement has same-volume and metadata/failure semantics.
sources.project_application: Separate atomic visibility from crash durability; do not infer a durable multi-file commit from a rename wrapper.

sources.title: Volume Shadow Copy Service
sources.verified_fact: VSS coordinates writers, requesters, and providers to create consistent snapshots; it is more than a directory notification facility.
sources.project_application: Consider only if a real point-in-time/application-consistent snapshot is required; a producer commit manifest may be simpler.

sources.title: TinyLFU: A Highly Efficient Cache Admission Policy
sources.author_or_publisher: Gil Einziger; Roy Friedman; Ben Manes
sources.verified_fact: Uses bounded recent approximate frequency and aging to decide admission relative to a potential eviction candidate; W-TinyLFU combines this with a window policy.
sources.project_application: Research baseline for scan-resistant admission; published trace results do not predict this catalog's latency.

sources.title: Lightweight Robust Size Aware Cache Management
sources.author_or_publisher: Gil Einziger; Ohad Eytan; Roy Friedman; Benjamin Manes
sources.verified_fact: Studies variable-size extensions; Aggregated Victims compares a candidate with the combined frequency of the full potential victim set before eviction.
sources.project_application: Large result admission should consider all displaced useful results, not just the first small victim.

sources.title: Cost-Aware WWW Proxy Caching Algorithms
sources.verified_fact: GreedyDual-Size combines recency/locality, retrieval cost, and object size in a cache replacement policy.
sources.project_application: Compare avoided compute cost per retained byte as well as hit ratio; do not transfer web-cache competitive or trace results to unmeasured ownership costs.

sources.title: Build Systems à la Carte: Theory and Practice
sources.author_or_publisher: Andrey Mokhov; Neil Mitchell; Simon Peyton Jones
sources.verified_fact: Separates scheduling and rebuilding decisions; describes traces, self-tracking, early cutoff, impurity, and inconsistent reuse of nondeterministic intermediates.
sources.project_application: Track rule/extractor and all dependency observations before selective reuse across generations; start whole-generation invalidation.

sources.title: Isolation In SQLite
sources.verified_fact: Separate connections normally see only complete committed transactions. WAL readers retain an unchanging database snapshot; writes are serialized.
sources.project_application: Optional durable metadata index; its transaction does not include arbitrary external payload files.

sources.title: Atomic Commit In SQLite
sources.verified_fact: Explains rollback-journal atomic commit and relevant filesystem, write-order, and flush assumptions; WAL uses another mechanism.
sources.project_application: Treat durable metadata publication as a protocol with explicit storage assumptions, and distinguish it from in-memory owner exchange.

sources.title: BY_HANDLE_FILE_INFORMATION
sources.verified_fact: File IDs are filesystem-specific, may be reused over time, and can change; ReFS requires 128-bit identity for its full identifier.
sources.project_application: Never make an indefinite cache key out of a bare file ID; digest captured content and bind to generation identity.

sources.title: SIEVE is Simpler than LRU: an Efficient Turn-Key Eviction Algorithm for Web Caches
sources.author_or_publisher: Yazhuo Zhang; Juncheng Yang; Yao Yue; Ymir Vigfusson; K. V. Rashmi
sources.verified_fact: Presents a simple cache eviction primitive and evaluates efficiency and hit-path scalability on web-cache traces.
sources.project_application: Potential later control if policy overhead or contention matters; no SIEVE result is measured for Suffice.

sources.title: FIFO Queues Are All You Need for Cache Eviction
sources.author_or_publisher: Juncheng Yang; Yazhuo Zhang; Ziyue Qiu; Yao Yue; K. V. Rashmi
sources.verified_fact: S3-FIFO uses three queues with a small filtering queue intended to demote one-hit objects quickly.
sources.project_application: Potential later scan-resistant control; measure full-session time and retained bytes rather than adopting published throughput ratios.
